drivingQuestion: Once an animal has been slaughtered, does it stand in a presumptive status of permissibility even when a doubt arises about it — and is uncertainty involving danger treated more stringently than uncertainty involving prohibition?
outcomeNote: The sugya concludes שמע מינה חמירא סכנתא מאיסורא, שמע מינה — Rav Huna's סכנה שאני is upheld against Rava's equation of danger with prohibition. The subsidiary questions (the knives, the vessels, the flanks, Shmuel's novelty, Rav Huna's wording, R' Abba's dilemma) are each answered in turn, and the closing מים מגולין material ends with the emended measure ישתה ויחזור לחורו.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הַטַּבָּח צָרִיךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה סַכִּינִין, אַחַת שֶׁשּׁוֹחֵט בָּהּ, וְאֶחָד שֶׁמְּחַתֵּךְ בָּהּ בָּשָׂר, וְאֶחָד שֶׁמְּחַתֵּךְ בָּהּ חֲלָבִים.
segments.en: § «Rav Yehuda says» that «Rav says: The slaughterer requires three knives, one with which he slaughters» the animal, «and one with which he cuts meat, and one with which he cuts» forbidden «fats.» One may not use the same knife for cutting the meat and the forbidden fats due to the residue on the knife after cutting the forbidden fats.

segments.he: וְלִיתַקֵּן לֵיהּ חֲדָא, וְלִיחְתּוֹךְ בָּהּ בָּשָׂר, וַהֲדַר לִיחְתּוֹךְ בַּהּ חֲלָבִים? גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַחְתּוֹךְ חֲלָבִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּשָׂר. הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי מִיחַלַּף לֵיהּ! כֵּיוָן דְּאַצְרְכִינְהוּ תְּרֵי – אִית לֵיהּ הֶיכֵּרָא.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «And let him designate one» knife for cutting both the meat and forbidden fats «and cut meat with it and then cut» forbidden «fats with it.» In this manner the forbidden residue on the knife will not affect the meat. The Gemara explains: The Sages issued a rabbinic «decree» prohibiting the use of one knife to cut meat and then forbidden fats «lest he» also «cut» forbidden «fats and cut meat thereafter.» The Gemara challenges: «Now too,» after the decree mandating separate knives there is a concern that «they will be confused for him» and he will use the knife that cut the forbidden fats to cut the meat. The Gemara explains: «Since» the Sages «required him» to have «two» knives, «he has a conspicuous marker» on one of the knives that will prevent confusion.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הַטַּבָּח צָרִיךְ שְׁנֵי כֵּלִים שֶׁל מַיִם, אֶחָד שֶׁמֵּדִיחַ בּוֹ בָּשָׂר, וְאֶחָד שֶׁמֵּדִיחַ בּוֹ חֲלָבִים. וְנִיתַקֵּן לֵיהּ חֲדָא, וּנְדִיחַ בּוֹ בָּשָׂר וַהֲדַר נְדִיחַ בּוֹ חֲלָבִים? גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יָדִיחַ חֲלָבִים וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּשָׂר. הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי מִיחַלְּפִי לֵיהּ? כֵּיוָן דְּאַצְרְכִינֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי אִית לֵיהּ הֶיכֵּרָא.
segments.en: «And Rav Yehuda says» that «Rav says: The slaughterer requires two vessels of water, one with which he rinses meat and one with which he rinses» forbidden «fats.» The Gemara suggests: «And let him designate one» vessel «and rinse meat with» the water in the vessel «and then rinse» forbidden «fats with» the water in the same vessel. The Gemara explains: The Sages issued a rabbinic «decree» to prohibit doing so «lest he rinse» fats «and rinse meat thereafter.» The Gemara challenges: «Now too,» after the decree mandating separate vessels there is a concern that «they will be confused for him» and he will rinse meat in the vessel in which he rinsed fats. The Gemara answers: «Since» the Sages «required him» to have «two» vessels, «he has a conspicuous marker» on one of the vessels that will prevent confusion.

segments.he: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא: לָא לִיסְחוֹף אִינִישׁ כַּפְלֵי עִילָּוֵי בִּישְׂרָא, דְּדָאֵיב תַּרְבָּא וּבָלַע בִּישְׂרָא.
segments.en: § «Ameimar says in the name of Rav Pappa: A person should not place [lisḥof] the flanks» of an animal «atop» other «meat» so that the forbidden fats that are attached to the flanks are in contact with the other meat, due to the fact «that the» forbidden «fat» liquefies and «flows and the meat absorbs» it.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, כִּי תְּרִיצִי נָמֵי דָּאֵיב תַּרְבָּא וּבָלַע בִּשְׂרָא? קְרָמָא מַפְסֵיק מִתַּתַּאי! אִי הָכִי
segments.en: The Gemara raises an objection: «If so,» and that is a concern, «when» the flanks are «placed» in their «typical» manner «[teritzi] as well,» with the forbidden fat above the meat of the flanks, «the» forbidden «fat flows and the meat» of the flanks «absorbs» it. The Gemara explains: «The membrane» between the forbidden fat and the meat of the flanks «interposes from below» and prevents absorption of the forbidden fat. The Gemara challenges: «If so,»

segments.he: מֵעִילַּאי נָמֵי קְרָמָא אִיכָּא? אַיְּידֵי דִּמְמַשְׁמְשָׁא יְדָא דְּטַבָּחָא מִפַּתַּת.
segments.en: «from above too there is a membrane» that should prevent the forbidden fat from flowing onto the piece of meat even if the forbidden fat is placed directly upon it. The Gemara explains: «Since the hand of the slaughterer touches» the upper membrane, that membrane «disintegrates» and the forbidden fat flows onto the meat.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּלְמוֹד שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים: כְּתָב, שְׁחִיטָה, וּמִילָה. וְרַב חֲנַנְיָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר: אַף קֶשֶׁר שֶׁל תְּפִילִּין, וּבִרְכַּת חֲתָנִים, וְצִיצִית. וְאִידַּךְ – הָנֵי שְׁכִיחָן.
segments.en: § «And Rav Yehuda says» that «Rav says: A Torah scholar is required to learn» the requisite skills to perform «three matters: Writing,» so that he will be able to write texts on various occasions, «ritual slaughter, and circumcision. And Rav Ḥananya bar Shelamya says in the name of Rav:» He must «also» learn to tie «the knot of the phylacteries, and» to recite «the blessing of the grooms» by heart and with the traditional intonation, «and» to tie «ritual fringes» to the corners of a garment. The Gemara notes: «And the other» amora, Rav Yehuda, holds that «those» skills «are commonplace» and do not require special training.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל טַבָּח שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ הִלְכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל מִשְּׁחִיטָתוֹ, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הִלְכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה: שְׁהִיָּיה, דְּרָסָה, חֲלָדָה, הַגְרָמָה, וְעִיקּוּר.
segments.en: § «And Rav Yehuda says» that «Shmuel says:» With regard to «any slaughterer who does not know the halakhot of ritual slaughter,» it is «prohibited to eat from his slaughter. And these are the halakhot of ritual slaughter: Interrupting» the slaughter, «pressing» the knife, «concealing» the knife under the windpipe or the gullet in the course of an inverted slaughter, «diverting» the knife from the place of slaughter, «and ripping» the simanim from their place before cutting them.

segments.he: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? כּוּלְּהוּ תְּנִינְהוּ! לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁשָּׁחַט לְפָנֵינוּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים וּשְׁחַט שַׁפִּיר; מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: מִדְּאִידַּךְ שְׁחַט שַׁפִּיר, הַאי נָמֵי שְׁחַט שַׁפִּיר, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא גְּמִר, זִימְנִין דְּשָׁהֵי וְדָרֵיס וְלָא יָדַע.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What» is the novelty in what Rav is «teaching us? We learned all of them» in the mishnayot in the second chapter of this tractate, and therefore it is obvious that a slaughterer who does not know these halakhot is not qualified. The Gemara answers: «No,» it is «necessary» in a case «where» the slaughterer «slaughtered before us twice or three times and slaughtered well. Lest you say: From» the fact «that he slaughtered the other» animals «well, this» animal «he also slaughtered well;» therefore, Rav «teaches us: Since he did not learn» the halakhot, «sometimes» it happens «that he interrupts» the slaughter «or presses» the knife, «and he does not know» that he invalidated the slaughter.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַטַּבָּח צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּבְדּוֹק בַּסִּימָנִים לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם שָׁהָה כְּדֵי בִּיקּוּר. מַאי לָאו כְּדֵי בִּיקּוּר סִימָנִין?
segments.en: § «And Rav Yehuda says» that «Shmuel says: The slaughterer must examine the simanim,» the windpipe and the gullet, «after» completing the «slaughter. Rav Yosef said: We learn» in a mishna (32a) «as well: Rabbi Shimon says:» The slaughter is not valid «if he interrupted» the slaughter for an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination. What, is it not» an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination of the simanim?» Apparently, one is obligated to examine the simanim.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּדֵי בִּיקּוּר חָכָם. אִם כֵּן, נָתַתָּ דְּבָרֶיךָ לְשִׁיעוּרִים! אֶלָּא, כְּדֵי בִּיקּוּר טַבָּח חָכָם.
segments.en: «Abaye said to him: No, this» is what «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» It is an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination» of the knife, as the Sages instituted that one must take the knife to be examined by a Torah «scholar» prior to slaughtering the animal. Rav Yosef said to him: «If so, you have rendered your statement» subject «to circumstances,» as sometimes the Torah scholar is near and sometimes the Torah scholar is far, and the time required for examination varies accordingly. «Rather,» it is an interval «equivalent» to the duration of «an examination» performed by «a slaughterer» who is a Torah «scholar.» In that case, the travel time is not factored, just the time of the examination, which does not vary.

segments.he: לֹא בָּדַק, מַאי? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: טְרֵפָה, וַאֲסוּרָה בַּאֲכִילָה. בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: נְבֵלָה, וּמְטַמְּאָה בְּמַשָּׂא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If the slaughterer «did not examine» the simanim after completing slaughter of the animal, «what» is the halakha? «Rabbi Eliezer ben Antigonus says in the name of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yannai:» The halakhic status of the slaughtered animal is that of «a tereifa, and it is forbidden for consumption,» but it does not impart impurity. «It was taught in a baraita:» Its halakhic status is that of «an unslaughtered carcass, and it imparts impurity by means of carrying» it.

segments.he: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? בִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר: בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ בְּחֶזְקַת אִיסּוּר עוֹמֶדֶת, עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע לָךְ בַּמֶּה נִשְׁחֲטָה. נִשְׁחֲטָה – הֲרֵי הִיא בְּחֶזְקַת הֶיתֵּר, עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע לָךְ בַּמֶּה נִטְרְפָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «With regard to what» principle «do they disagree?» The Gemara answers: They disagree «with regard to» the application of the halakha stated by «Rav Huna, who says: An animal during its lifetime exists with the presumptive status of prohibition,» as it is prohibited to eat a living animal, and it continues to have this status even after its death «until it will become known to you in what» manner «it was slaughtered,» i.e., whether it was properly slaughtered. Once the animal «was slaughtered,» it exists «with the presumptive status of permissibility until it will become known to you in what» manner «it was rendered a tereifa.»

segments.he: מָר סָבַר: בְּחֶזְקַת אִיסּוּר קָיְימָא, וְהַשְׁתָּא מֵתָה הִיא; וּמָר סָבַר: בְּחֶזְקַת אִיסּוּר אָמְרִינַן, בְּחֶזְקַת טוּמְאָה לָא אָמְרִינַן.
segments.en: It is with regard to the application of this halakha that Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yannai, and the tanna of the baraita disagree in a case where the slaughterer did not examine the simanim after completing the slaughter. One «Sage holds:» Since it has not been verified that the animal was slaughtered properly, the animal «exists with the presumptive status of prohibition, and» since «now it is dead,» it assumes the status of an unslaughtered carcass and imparts impurity. «And» one «Sage holds: With» regard to «the presumptive status of prohibition, we say» that the animal is forbidden until it is verified that it was slaughtered properly; «with regard to the presumptive status of ritual impurity we do not say» that the animal is impure, as a living animal is not ritually impure.

segments.he: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ בְּחֶזְקַת אִיסּוּר עוֹמֶדֶת עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע לָךְ בַּמֶּה נִשְׁחֲטָה, נִשְׁחֲטָה – בְּחֶזְקַת הֶיתֵּר עוֹמֶדֶת עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע לָךְ בַּמֶּה נִטְרְפָה. וְלֵימָא: ״נִשְׁחֲטָה הוּתְּרָה״! הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיתְיְלִיד בַּהּ רֵיעוּתָא.
segments.en: § The Gemara proceeds to analyze «the» matter «itself. Rav Huna says: An animal during its lifetime exists with the presumptive status of prohibition until it will become known to you in what» manner «it was slaughtered.» Once the animal «was slaughtered, it exists with the presumptive status of permissibility until it will become known to you in what» manner «it was rendered a tereifa.» The Gemara challenges this: «And let us say» that once the animal «was slaughtered, it became permitted,» instead of saying that it exists with the presumptive status of permissibility. The Gemara explains: «This teaches us that even if a flaw developed in» the animal that raises uncertainty with regard to its permitted status, it retains its presumptive status of permissibility.

segments.he: כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא מֵרַב הוּנָא: בָּא זְאֵב וְנָטַל בְּנֵי מֵעַיִם, מַהוּ?
segments.en: «As Rabbi Abba raised a dilemma before Rav Huna:» If «a wolf came and took» the «innards» of a slaughtered animal, «what is» the halakha?

segments.he: נָטַל?! הָא לֵיתַנְהוּ, אֶלָּא נָקַב בְּנֵי מֵעַיִים מַהוּ? נָקַב?! הָא קָא חָזֵינַן דְּהוּא נַקְבִינְהוּ! אֶלָּא נְטָלָן וְהֶחְזִירָן כְּשֶׁהֵן נְקוּבִין, מַהוּ? מִי חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב נָקַב, אוֹ לָא?
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Took?» In that case the innards «are not» there, and therefore there is no way of seeing an indication of a flaw. «Rather,» the dilemma is: In a case where a wolf «perforated the innards» of a slaughtered animal, «what is» the halakha? The Gemara challenges: «Perforated? We see that» the wolf «perforated them» and in that case too there is no indication of a flaw. «Rather,» the dilemma is: In a case where a wolf «took» the innards «and returned them when they are perforated, what is» the halakha? «Are we concerned» that «perhaps» the wolf «perforated» the innards «in the place of» a preexisting «perforation» and the animal was a tereifa from the outset, «or» is that possibility «not» a concern?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב נָקַב.
segments.en: Rav Huna «said to» Rabbi Abba: «One is not concerned» that «perhaps» the wolf «perforated» the innards «in the place of» a preexisting «perforation,» because one relies on the presumptive status of permissibility.

segments.he: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: רָאָה צִפּוֹר הַמְנַקֵּר בִּתְאֵנָה וְעַכְבָּר הַמְנַקֵּר בָּאֲבַטִּיחִים,
segments.en: Rabbi Abba «raised an objection to» the opinion of Rav Huna: If «one saw a bird pecking at a fig or a mouse gnawing at melons,»

segments.he: חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בִּמְקוֹם נֶקֶב נָקַב.
segments.en: «one is concerned that perhaps» the bird or the mouse «perforated» it «in the place of» the preexisting «perforation» caused by a snake, and it is prohibited to eat the fig or the melon, due to the danger that the snake might have left its venom.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי קָא מְדַמֵּית אִיסּוּרָא לְסַכַּנְתָּא? סַכָּנָה שָׁאנֵי! אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מַאי שְׁנָא? סְפֵק סַכַּנְתָּא לְחוּמְרָא? סְפֵק אִיסּוּרָא נָמֵי לְחוּמְרָא!
segments.en: Rav Huna «said to» Rabbi Abba: «Are you comparing danger to prohibition? Danger is different,» and one rules stringently in cases involving danger. «Rava said to him: What is different» about the fact that the ruling in cases of «uncertainty» involving «danger» is «stringent,» given that in cases of «uncertainty» involving «prohibition» the ruling is «also stringent?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְלָא שָׁאנֵי בֵּין אִיסּוּרָא לְסַכַּנְתָּא? וְהָא אִילּוּ סְפֵק טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים – סְפֵיקוֹ טָהוֹר, וְאִילּוּ סְפֵק מַיִם מְגוּלִּין – אֲסוּרִין!
segments.en: «Abaye said to» Rava: «And is there no difference between prohibition and danger? But isn’t» it the halakha that in a case of «uncertainty» involving «ritual impurity in the public domain, its uncertain» impurity leaves it «pure, while» in a case of «uncertainty» involving «water» that is «exposed» and therefore susceptible to a snake leaving venom in it, the water is «forbidden.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ מִסּוֹטָה, מָה סוֹטָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד – אַף טוּמְאָה בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד.
segments.en: Rava «said to» Abaye: «There,» in the case of ritual impurity in the public domain, the Sages «learned this halakha through tradition from» the case of «a sota,» a woman who enters into seclusion with a particular man after her husband warns her not to. She is forbidden to her husband even though there is uncertainty whether or not she committed adultery. «Just as a sota is» forbidden only in a case of uncertainty «in the private domain,» as there is no seclusion in the public domain; «so too» with regard to «ritual impurity,» one becomes ritually impure in a case of uncertainty only «in the private domain.»

segments.he: מֵתִיב רַב שִׁימִי: שֶׁרֶץ בְּפִי חוּלְדָּה, וְחוּלְדָּה מְהַלֶּכֶת עַל גַּבֵּי כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה – סָפֵק נָגַע, סָפֵק לֹא נָגַע – סְפֵיקוֹ טָהוֹר, וְאִילּוּ סְפֵק מַיִם מְגוּלִּין אֲסוּרִין!
segments.en: «Rav Shimi raises an objection» to the opinion of Rava from a mishna (Teharot 4:2): If the carcass of «a creeping animal» was «in the mouth of a weasel, and» that «weasel» was «walking on loaves of teruma,» and there is «uncertainty» whether the creeping animal «touched» the loaves and «uncertainty» whether it «did not touch» the loaves, «its uncertain» impurity leaves it «pure, while» in a case of «uncertainty» involving «water» that is «exposed» and therefore susceptible to a snake leaving venom in it, the water is «forbidden.»

segments.he: הָתָם נָמֵי הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ מִסּוֹטָה: מָה סוֹטָה דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל, אַף הָכָא נָמֵי דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «There too, the halakha is derived from» the case of «a sota. Just as» the uncertainty in the case of «sota» involves «an entity that has consciousness» in order for her «to be asked» whether she was unfaithful and is forbidden to her husband, «so too here,» only uncertainty involving «an entity that has consciousness» in order for it «to be asked» whether the loaves were rendered impure would become impure. The weasel does not have that consciousness.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע: צְלוֹחִית שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ מְגוּלָּה וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ מְכוּסָּה – טְמֵאָה, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם טָמֵא נִכְנַס לְשָׁם וְכִיסָּהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said: Come» and «hear» additional proof that danger is more severe than prohibition (see mishna Para 11:1): In the case of «a flask» of purification water «that one left exposed and he came» back «and found it covered,» it is «ritually impure, as I say: An impure man entered into there and covered» it, and in the course of doing so he rendered the vessel and its contents impure.

segments.he: הִנִּיחָהּ מְכוּסָּה וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ מְגוּלָּה, אִם יְכוֹלָה חוּלְדָּה לִשְׁתּוֹת מִמֶּנָּה, אוֹ נָחָשׁ לְדִבְרֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אוֹ שֶׁיָּרַד בָּהּ טַל בַּלַּיְלָה – פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: In a case where «one left» the vessel «covered and came» back «and found it exposed, if» it is in a place where «a weasel could drink from it, or a snake according to the statement of Rabban Gamliel, or» if there is concern «that dew fell into it at night,» the purification waters are «disqualified» for sprinkling in the process of purification of a person impure with impurity imparted by a corpse, due to the concern that the saliva of the weasel or the dew, which are unfit for sprinkling, intermingled with it. Nevertheless, the water is not impure.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מָה טַעַם?
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: What is the reason» that there is no concern that a ritually impure person exposed the waters and rendered them impure?

segments.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁדַּרְכָּן שֶׁל שְׁרָצִים לְגַלּוֹת, וְאֵין דַּרְכָּן לְכַסּוֹת.
segments.en: It is «due to» the fact «that it is» the typical «manner of creeping animals to expose» the contents of a vessel so that they may drink. Therefore, the exposure of the water is attributed to a creeping animal or to a ritually pure person. By contrast, in a case where he left the vessel exposed and found it covered, the concern is that it was an impure man who covered it, since «it is not» the typical «manner of» creeping animals «to cover» exposed vessels. Evidently, with regard to prohibition or ritual impurity, there are circumstances of uncertainty when the ruling is lenient.

segments.he: אִי נָמֵי, טַעְמָא דְּהִנִּיחָהּ מְגוּלָּה וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ מְכוּסָּה, מְכוּסָּה וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ מְגוּלָּה, הָא מְצָאָהּ כְּמָה שֶׁהִנִּיחָהּ – לָא טוּמְאָה אִיכָּא וְלָא פְּסוּלָא אִיכָּא.
segments.en: «Alternatively,» it can be inferred from the baraita that «the reason» the contents of the vessel are impure or disqualified, respectively, is «that he left it exposed and came» back «and found it covered» or that he left it «covered and came» back «and found it exposed. But» if «he found» the vessel just «as he left it, there is neither impurity nor disqualification.»

segments.he: וְאִילּוּ סְפֵק מַיִם מְגוּלִּים אֲסוּרִין, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: חֲמִירָא סַכַּנְתָּא מֵאִיסּוּרָא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: «But» in a situation of «uncertainty» where he left «exposed water» and then came and found the vessel exposed, the water is «forbidden» under all circumstances. «Learn from it» that «danger is more severe than prohibition.» The Gemara affirms: Indeed, «learn from it.»

segments.he: תְּנַן הָתָם: שְׁלֹשָׁה מַשְׁקִין אֲסוּרִין מִשּׁוּם גִּלּוּי – מַיִם, וְיַיִן, וְחָלָב. כַּמָּה יִשְׁהוּ וְיִהְיוּ אֲסוּרִין? כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא הָרַחַשׁ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב וְיִשְׁתֶּה. וְכַמָּה מָקוֹם קָרוֹב? אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִתַּחַת אוֹזֶן כְּלִי וְיִשְׁתֶּה.
segments.en: «We learned» in a mishna «there» (Terumot 8:4): «Three liquids are forbidden due to exposure: Water, wine, and milk. How long shall they remain» exposed «and» their contents «will be forbidden?» It is a period «equivalent» to the time necessary so «that a snake could emerge from a proximate place and drink. And how» far away is considered «a proximate place? Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Yehuda, said:» Even a period «equivalent» to the time necessary «so that» a snake «could emerge from beneath the handle of the vessel and drink.»

segments.he: יִשְׁתֶּה? הָא קָא חָזֵי לֵיהּ! אֶלָּא, יִשְׁתֶּה וְיַחֲזוֹר לְחוֹרוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If it is only the time necessary for the snake to emerge and «drink, doesn’t one see» the snake drink, in which case there is no uncertainty? «Rather,» it is a period equivalent to the time necessary for a snake to emerge from a proximate place, «drink, and return to its hole.» If one left exposed liquid unattended for that interval, it is possible that the snake drank the liquid unseen by the owner of the liquid.

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda transmits Rav's ruling that a slaughterer needs three knives.
moves.about: Rav's ruling that a slaughterer requires three knives

moves.summary: Why not one knife, used for meat first and forbidden fats after?
moves.about: why three knives are needed rather than one knife used for meat first and forbidden fats afterward

moves.cueHe: גזירה שמא יחתוך חלבים ואחר כך בשר
moves.summary: A decree, lest he reverse the order and cut meat after fats.
moves.about: why one knife does not suffice — a decree lest he reverse the order and cut meat after fats

moves.summary: Two knives can be confused for one another just the same.
moves.about: whether two knives still leave room for the very confusion the decree feared

moves.summary: Being required to keep two is itself the marker that prevents confusion.
moves.about: requiring two knives is itself the conspicuous marker that prevents confusion

moves.summary: The same tradent brings Rav's parallel ruling on two vessels of water.
moves.about: Rav's ruling that a slaughterer requires two vessels of water

moves.summary: Why not one vessel, meat first and fats after?
moves.about: why two vessels are needed rather than one used for meat first and fats afterward

moves.cueHe: גזירה שמא ידיח חלבים ואחר כך בשר
moves.summary: A decree lest he rinse fats and then meat.
moves.about: a decree lest he rinse fats and then meat in the same vessel

moves.summary: The two vessels may themselves be confused.
moves.about: whether the two vessels may themselves be confused for one another

moves.summary: The requirement of two is itself the marker.
moves.about: being required to keep two vessels is itself the marker that prevents confusion

moves.summary: Ameimar transmits Rav Pappa: do not lay flanks fat-side-down on meat, since the fat flows and is absorbed.
moves.about: Rav Pappa's ruling not to lay the flanks fat-side-down upon other meat

moves.summary: Then flanks laid the normal way should also absorb their own fat.
moves.about: if liquefied fat is absorbed, flanks laid in the ordinary way should also have their own meat absorb the forbidden fat

moves.summary: A membrane below interposes.
moves.about: a membrane below interposes between the forbidden fat and the meat of the flanks

moves.summary: There is a membrane above too, which should equally block the fat.
moves.about: if a membrane blocks from below, the membrane above should equally block the fat from reaching the meat beneath

moves.summary: The upper membrane disintegrates under the slaughterer's handling.
moves.about: the upper membrane disintegrates under the slaughterer's handling

moves.summary: Rav: a Torah scholar must learn writing, slaughter and circumcision.
moves.about: Rav's ruling that a Torah scholar must learn writing, slaughter and circumcision

moves.cueHe: ורב חנניא בר שלמיא משמיה דרב אמר
moves.summary: A rival version of Rav's list adds the knot of phylacteries, the grooms' blessing and fringes.
moves.about: Rav's ruling as Rav Ḥananya received it, adding the knot of phylacteries, the grooms' blessing and ritual fringes

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda omits them because those skills are commonplace.
moves.about: why Rav Yehuda's version of Rav's list omits those three skills — they are commonplace and need no special training

moves.summary: Shmuel: one may not eat from the slaughter of an ignorant slaughterer; the five disqualifications are listed.
moves.about: Shmuel's ruling that one may not eat from the slaughter of a slaughterer who does not know the halakhot of slaughter

moves.cueHe: מאי קא משמע לן? כולהו תנינהו
moves.summary: The mishnayot already teach all five, so what is the novelty?
moves.about: whether Shmuel's list of the halakhot of slaughter adds anything, since the mishnayot already teach all five

moves.summary: One who never learned may interrupt or press without knowing it.
moves.about: rejecting the supposition that past good slaughters vouch for this one — one who never learned may interrupt or press without knowing it

moves.summary: It is needed where he already slaughtered well before us several times.
moves.about: the ruling is needed where the slaughterer already slaughtered well before us two or three times

moves.summary: One might have said his earlier good slaughters vouch for this one.
moves.about: the mishnayot of the second chapter already teach the five disqualifications of slaughter

moves.summary: Shmuel: the slaughterer must examine the simanim after slaughter.
moves.about: Shmuel's ruling that the slaughterer must examine the simanim after slaughter

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יוסף: אף אנן נמי תנינא
moves.summary: Rav Yosef adduces R' Shimon's mishna about interrupting כדי ביקור as support.
moves.about: the mishna teaching that an interruption of the length of an examination invalidates the slaughter

moves.summary: He reads כדי ביקור as the time to examine the simanim.
moves.about: R' Shimon's measure of כדי ביקור for an interruption during slaughter

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי: לא, הכי אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Abaye dismisses the reading: R' Yoḥanan said it means the time to have the knife examined by a scholar.
moves.about: whether the mishna's כדי ביקור refers to examining the simanim rather than to having the knife examined by a scholar

moves.summary: That measure varies with the scholar's distance.
moves.about: whether כדי ביקור חכם yields a measure that varies with how far away the scholar is

moves.summary: Rather, the time an expert slaughterer takes to examine his own knife.
moves.about: the measure is the time an expert slaughterer takes to examine his own knife, which does not vary

moves.summary: What if he did not examine the simanim?
moves.about: the status of an animal whose simanim were not examined after slaughter, given Shmuel's requirement to examine them

moves.cueHe: רבי אליעזר בן אנטיגנוס משום רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי אמר
moves.summary: A tereifa, forbidden for consumption.
moves.about: that the unexamined slaughtered animal is a tereifa, forbidden for consumption but not conveying impurity

moves.summary: A baraita rules it a carcass that imparts impurity by carrying.
moves.about: a baraita ruling the unexamined animal a carcass that imparts impurity by carrying

moves.summary: What principle divides them?
moves.about: the principle underlying the dispute over the unexamined animal

moves.summary: They divide over Rav Huna's rule of presumptive status before and after slaughter.
moves.about: Rav Huna's rule that an animal stands in presumptive prohibition while alive and in presumptive permissibility once slaughtered

moves.summary: One holds the presumption of prohibition makes the dead animal a carcass; the other says presumptive impurity is never asserted.
moves.about: that the animal remains in its presumptive prohibited status and, being now dead, has the status of a carcass

moves.summary: Rav Huna's dictum is taken up in its own right.
moves.about: returning to Rav Huna's statement itself in order to analyse its wording

moves.summary: Why not say simply that once slaughtered it became permitted?
moves.about: why Rav Huna said the slaughtered animal stands in presumptive permissibility rather than simply that it became permitted

moves.summary: The wording teaches that the presumption survives a flaw.
moves.about: Rav Huna's wording teaches that the presumption of permissibility holds even after a flaw has arisen

moves.cueHe: כדבעא מיניה רבי אבא מרב הונא
moves.summary: R' Abba asks Rav Huna about an animal whose innards a wolf took.
moves.about: the status of a slaughtered animal after a wolf took its innards

moves.summary: If the wolf took them away there is nothing to examine.
moves.about: the dilemma cannot concern innards the wolf carried off, since they are no longer here to be examined

moves.summary: The dilemma is restated as a wolf perforating the innards.
moves.about: if we saw the wolf perforate them there is no uncertainty at all

moves.cueHe: נקב?! הא קא חזינן דהוא נקבינהו
moves.summary: If we watched it perforate, there is no uncertainty.
moves.about: restating the dilemma as a case where the wolf perforated the innards

moves.cueHe: אלא נטלן והחזירן כשהן נקובין, מהו
moves.summary: The real dilemma: it took them and returned them perforated — do we suspect a preexisting hole?
moves.about: the dilemma is where the wolf took the innards and returned them perforated, so one cannot tell whether it perforated at the site of an existing hole

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אין חוששין שמא במקום נקב נקב
moves.summary: Rav Huna: we do not suspect it, relying on the presumption of permissibility.
moves.about: whether we suspect the wolf perforated at the site of a preexisting perforation

moves.summary: A source says one IS concerned that a bird pecked at the site of a snake's hole.
moves.about: a tannaitic ruling that one IS concerned a bird or mouse pecked at the site of a snake's preexisting perforation

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: מי קא מדמית איסורא לסכנתא
moves.summary: That case is danger, which is different from prohibition.
moves.about: the fig and melon case involves danger, which is not comparable to prohibition

moves.summary: Rava: uncertainty is ruled stringently in both, so what is the difference?
moves.about: whether uncertainty about danger is any more stringent than uncertainty about prohibition, since both are ruled stringently

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה אביי: ולא שאני בין איסורא לסכנתא
moves.summary: Uncertain impurity in the public domain is pure, yet uncertainly exposed water is forbidden.
moves.about: whether prohibition and danger are treated alike under uncertainty — uncertain impurity in the public domain is pure, while uncertainly exposed water is forbidden

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: התם הלכתא גמירי לה מסוטה
moves.summary: That leniency is a received derivation from sota, limited to the private domain.
moves.about: the leniency for uncertain impurity in the public domain is a special received derivation from sota, not a general rule about prohibition

moves.summary: Loaves under a weasel are pure under uncertainty even in the private domain.
moves.about: whether the sota derivation can account for loaves of teruma being pure under uncertainty even in the private domain

moves.cueHe: התם נמי הלכתא גמירי לה מסוטה
moves.summary: The sota derivation also limits impurity to an entity with awareness to be asked.
moves.about: the sota derivation also restricts uncertain impurity to an entity that has the awareness to be asked

moves.summary: Rav Ashi brings the mishna of the flask of purification water as proof that danger is more severe.
moves.about: the mishna about a flask of purification water left exposed and found covered, or left covered and found exposed

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: מה טעם
moves.summary: Why is there no concern that an impure person uncovered it?
moves.about: why we do not suspect that a ritually impure person uncovered the flask

moves.summary: Creeping animals uncover vessels but do not cover them.
moves.about: the mishna's ruling rests on the fact that creeping animals uncover vessels but do not cover them

moves.summary: Alternatively: found as left, there is neither impurity nor disqualification.
moves.about: the mishna's precision implies that a flask found exactly as it was left is neither impure nor disqualified

moves.summary: Conclude that danger is more severe than prohibition, and the conclusion is affirmed.
moves.about: that danger is more severe than prohibition, since uncertainly exposed water is forbidden in every case

moves.summary: By association, the mishna on three liquids forbidden because of exposure is brought.
moves.about: the mishna in Terumot listing the three liquids forbidden on account of exposure

moves.summary: How near is a proximate place?
moves.about: how near counts as a proximate place from which a snake could emerge to drink

moves.cueHe: אמר רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה
moves.summary: Even from beneath the handle of the vessel.
moves.about: the measure of a proximate place — even from beneath the handle of the vessel

moves.summary: If the measure ends at drinking, one would have seen it and there is no uncertainty.
moves.about: if the measure ends when the snake drinks, the owner would have seen it drink and there would be no uncertainty at all

moves.summary: Rather, the time to drink and return to its hole unseen.
moves.about: the measure is the time for the snake to drink and return to its hole unseen
